hypothesis: Across well-recorded classes of animals and plants, most genera (and a larger share of genera than of families) have essentially all of their modern occurrence records within a single continental region; and among mammal genera, those whose species are most closely related (youngest crown age in a dated phylogeny) occupy fewer regions and are more often confined to a single region than genera whose species are more distantly related.
pass_criterion: Clause 1 (regional confinement by rank): in each of the analysed classes (Mammalia, Aves, Amphibia, Reptilia, Magnoliopsida, Liliopsida, Pinopsida; GBIF backbone), the fraction of assessable genera that are confined to one region (>= 95% of their continent-assigned, non-fossil, non-captive occurrence records in one of six regions: Africa, Eurasia, North America, South America, Oceania, Antarctica) is > 0.50 in at least five of the seven classes, and in at least five of seven classes the confined fraction for genera exceeds the confined fraction for families. Clause 2 (natural genera are local, mammals): the Spearman partial correlation between genus crown age (MRCA age of the sampled congeneric species in the Upham et al. 2019 DNA-only MCC tree) and the number of regions holding >= 5% of the genus's records, controlling for log(number of sampled species in the genus), is positive with p < 0.05, AND the single-region fraction among genera in the youngest crown-age tercile exceeds that in the oldest tercile. The claim is 'supports' if both clauses pass; 'mixed' if exactly one passes; 'refutes' if both fail.
fail_criterion: Clause 1 fails if the confined fraction of genera is <= 0.50 in three or more of the seven classes, or genera are not more confined than families in three or more classes. Clause 2 fails if the partial Spearman correlation between crown age and number of regions is <= 0 or not significant at p < 0.05, or the youngest-tercile single-region fraction does not exceed the oldest-tercile fraction. Both clauses failing refutes the claim.
interpretation: Darwin's 'region' is read as a continental biogeographic region (six regions, with Europe and Asia merged into Eurasia following Sclater's Palaearctic). 'Confined to a single region' is read with a 5% tolerance for misidentified, vagrant, introduced or mislabelled records. Sub-families and sections of genera are not available in the GBIF backbone and are not tested; the rank gradient is tested only between family and genus, with species reported as an extra. 'Most natural genera (species most closely related)' is read, following the assessors, as genera with the youngest crown age in a dated molecular phylogeny; this is a modern phylogenetic reinterpretation of a pre-evolutionary taxonomic notion. Only genera with >= 20 qualifying occurrence records are assessed, so that poorly recorded taxa do not appear confined merely through lack of records.
